topic.title: The sample flat is built to lie politely
topic.claim: A sample flat isn't a preview of your home; it's a set, built so small rooms look big.
topic.moment: Walking through a show flat with soft lights, a narrow bed and no wardrobe doors open.

turn.believed: The sample flat shows what you'll get.
turn.actually: Furniture is chosen and placed to hide how tight the rooms are.

topic.because: You decide with your eyes, not a tape measure. A builder only needs you to feel space for ten minutes.
topic.payoff: Carry a tape. Measure where your own double bed would go. That's the real flat.
topic.behaviour: Buyers fall for staged flats; builders style them with slim furniture and mirrors.
topic.mechanism: A feeling of space sells faster than square feet on paper.
topic.group: First-time flat buyers in their late 20s and 30s
topic.send_to: The friend who just booked a flat after one site visit.
topic.why_now: Festive launches and 'Diwali offers' bring a wave of site visits.

score.why: The sample flat is a set; the tape-measure test is saveable and ties to the flat-costs-a-decade theme.
